newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates lowest in more than eight months.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates lowest in more than eight months.

text.p: Home mortgage rates fell last week to their lowest levels since the first week in March, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
It said rates on 30-year fixed-rate mortgages fell for the fifth consecutive week to 7.53 percent from 7.59 percent -- their lowest since 7.38 percent in the week ended March 8.
Rates on 15-year fixed-rate loans also fell to an average 7.06 percent from 7.11 percent last week. That was the lowest since 6.87 percent in the March 8 week.

One-year adjustable-rate mortgages inched down to 5.48 percent on average, the lowest rate since 5.40 percent in the week ended March 8. The previous week, one-year adjustable rates stood at 5.52 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.35 percent, the 15-year loan stood at 6.85 percent, and the one-year adjustable mortgage was at 5.61 percent.

"Since there is little fear this week that inflation will rise or the Fed will raise rates anytime soon, interest rates declined slightly for the fifth week in a row," Freddie Mac chief economist Robert Van Order said.

The agency said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans and 1.4 percent on ARM loans, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year mortgages, down from 1.8 percent last week.
